hardFailures: Essential content unreadable: beat 1's payoff — the product's own detail card carrying '#30 Completed · grading: passed', the only line that links the clicked Editor token to the certificate that follows — measures 8px cap height for the outcome line and 10px for 'Editor MEMBER' inside a 1080px-wide frame (bright-pixel row extents 1874-1881 and 1832-1841 in frame 98). At the 390px phone downscale I rendered it is an illegible grey smudge, ~3px cap height. Round 4's claimed punch-in does not exist: I measured the card's text row extents in frames 45, 60, 75, 90 and 98 and got identical results (54 text rows spanning y=1795-1919 in every one), so the card is pixel-identical in size for the whole 1.5s-3.27s stretch while the office camera behind it enlarges ~1.55x.

Major dead travel: 31.1% of the 315 frames (98 frames) change by less than 0.10/255 mean luminance from the previous frame, and 41.0% by less than 0.30. The three runs are t=0.07-1.00 (the clip opens on a still office; the only thing moving is a ~36px cursor glyph that travels 22px total and then stops dead from t=0.43 to t=0.87), t=5.20-6.80 (1.63s in which the entire 1080x1920 certificate frame is frozen and the sole moving object is a ~28x40px cursor), and t=9.43-10.47 (1.07s in which consecutive frames are bit-identical, mean diff exactly 0.000). That is 3.67s of a 10.5s clip with no visible frame change beyond a cursor.
notes: Beat 1 is authentic and unmodified: I compared candidate frame 0 and frame 27 against frames 0 and 27 of public/footage/office-beat.mp4 and got mean absolute RGB difference 1.31 and 1.38 with a single pixel above threshold 25 — codec noise only. The 'HANDSEL · OFFICE' header, the LIVE dot, the cyan token rings, ENG.FLOOR / QA.REDTEAM slugs and the bottom detail card all come from the product's own renderer, not from the video.

Round 4's fabricated URL strip is genuinely gone. I sampled the bottom 25 rows of every 15th frame: through beats 2 and 3 the bottom band reads RGB ~[238,245,241] to [253,253,253], i.e. the certificate/JSON page ground, with no dark chrome band and no address text anywhere in the clip.

Every on-screen value traces to the research brief. Frame 204 renders 작업 #30, 판정 ✅ 채점 통과, 워커 l6F52Ds58-pd7uhMbWtuc, 요청자 DrEZEVRWLVfdbIMEHgsH8, 지문 0x5b44eef1…a37af6df, 발급자 0x81C76907…7a3D3B68, CID bafkreib45…lxtxno4e, 서명 검증 유효 ✓ — and I confirmed the same rows in the same order in the source capture public/research/page-certificate.png. No row is added, removed or reworded. Frames 205 and 300 show the raw JSON with verdict pass, gradedAt 1787886796, the 65-byte signature and "verify":"/api/attestation", all matching the brief. I found no invented metric, verdict, name or claim anywhere in the clip.

The certificate press produces literally no response from the page — round 4's defect is unrepaired. Differencing frame 203 against frame 196 at full resolution, exactly 164 pixels change in the entire 2,073,600-pixel frame, bounded to (421,1861)-(446,1887): that box is only the cursor arrow scaling down about 10%. The green footer link 「원본 JSON으로 직접 검증 →」 does not change colour, weight, underline or position. I cropped and 5x-magnified the link before and after the press and they are identical apart from the arrow glyph.

That press is also invisible at destination size. In the 390px downscale of frame 204 the footer link sits at roughly 5px cap height in the bottom 6% of the frame; a phone viewer cannot see the actor, the target, or the act. The clip's second causal event therefore only exists at 1080px.

Beat 1's causality does work and is the strongest thing here: the cursor arrives, the Editor token's selection ring brightens at frame 27 (2,801 pixels change versus frame 20, bounded to the token and its ring), the product's camera starts flying in at frame 31 (t=1.03) and the detail card follows. The press is now on screen rather than before frame one. But it is preceded by 0.9s of a static establishing frame, which is empty travel before action.

Round 4's amputated establishing shot is unrepaired. In frame 0 the right edge cuts 'Independent Ch[eck]' and 'VERIFY.CO[URT]' mid-word, and 'Fact Checl' is both clipped and overlapped by the Red Team token. Three of the five room/agent labels in the opening frame are broken.

Beat 2's camera energy is genuinely fixed — the cut at frame 99 (mean diff 182) opens tight on the verified banner and the pull-back runs frames 100-155 with per-frame mean diffs peaking at 14.8, a real, large, motivated move rather than round 4's 68px drift. But it completes 1.63s before the beat ends and the frame then sits still.

Mid-pullback composition is poor. Frame 120 (t=4.00) has an empty white band roughly 650px tall through the middle of the frame (~34% of frame height) while the row labels are cut off the left edge ('…자)', '…문 (keccak256)') and the values are cut off the right ('l6F52Ds58-pd7uh…', 'DrEZEVRWLVfdbIM…'). Both edges amputate text simultaneously.

Beat 3 still has no dominant value — round 4's defect stands. It runs t=6.83-10.50, 3.67s, 34.9% of the clip, and every character is the same monospace weight and size. The reference's defining discipline is one huge legible value per hold (98 / 97 / 96 becoming 42 / 39 / 36 in reference-frames-1fps.jpg); here 'pass' is set identically to the 130-character signature beside it. Nothing in the last third is emphasised, and the final held frame carries no Handsel identity beyond the string 'a":"handsel.work.v1' clipped at the top edge.

The clip does not inherit the reference's core mechanism. smartlead-prewarmed-burn earns its motion by returning to the same three account cards and showing their state changed. This candidate shows three different surfaces once each and never revisits one, so 'system state changed as a consequence' is carried entirely by a hard cut to a replacement page rather than by anything visibly changing on screen.

Beat 3's travel also judders into its ending. From frame 268 the per-frame diff quantises to a repeating 5.38 / 10.61 / 0.000 pattern (frames 278, 280, 281, 283 and 284 are bit-identical to their predecessors), i.e. the scroll drops below one pixel per frame and stutters into the freeze rather than decelerating smoothly.

Material restraint is good and I found nothing to fault. No neon, bloom, coloured shadow, gradient wash or glassmorphism is added anywhere; comparing candidate frame 0 to the source recording gives mean RGB difference 1.31, so no grade, vignette or glow was laid over the capture. The cyan token rings and monitor light are inside the product's own painted renderer. No drawn certificate, receipt, stamp, floating card or card grid appears — the only certificate on screen is the product's real page.

Omitting handsel-logo.svg is defensible and I do not score it as an identity failure: the wordmark appears inside two authentic captured surfaces ('HANDSEL · OFFICE' in beat 1, 'HANDSEL · PROOF OF AUTHORSHIP & GRADE' in beat 2), both rendered by the product itself.
